0.2.0.lead: Signing in works with several providers at once, and changing the public address asks before it takes effect.

sections.title: Several providers, one button each
sections.body: Offer as many OpenID Connect providers as you like, for example authentik and Microsoft Entra ID, each with its own button. A person links an account per provider, and signing in follows the link, never the mail address. Accounts that were found by their address before are linked already.

sections.title: Asked before it changes
sections.body: The authentik button asks first when it would hand the links to another issuer. Changing the public address asks as well, because the return address of every provider depends on it.

sections.title: Keys wait for a second factor
sections.body: While a required second factor is still missing for your account, your API keys wait, and the list of keys says so.

small: Behind a reverse proxy, NEXBRAND_TRUSTED_PROXIES now also decides whether the scheme sent by the proxy is believed. Without it the return address of the sign-in is asked for and never guessed.
Mails carry a Date header now, some providers dropped them without one.

0.1.1.lead: Signing in stands up better to strangers, and the authentik button finds its own provider again after a move.

sections.title: Signing in stands up better to strangers
sections.body: Whoever guesses passwords now waits themselves. A browser you signed in with before still gets in, even when someone from the same address tried wrong passwords for your very sign-in name.

sections.title: authentik after a move
sections.where: Settings, Server, Sign-in, “authentik in one step”
sections.body: When nexbrand moves to a new address, the button finds the provider in authentik that belongs to this nexbrand again, also when it was renamed there. The accounts keep their sign-in, and a second nexbrand on the same authentik keeps its own provider.

small: Where the sign-in name is meant, it is called that now: on the sign-in page, under My account and in the message after a wrong password.
A mail address with an invisible control character is refused.
A damaged browser cookie no longer leads to an error when signing in.

0.1.0.lead: The first version of nexbrand: your clients' corporate design in one place, with every version, the checks that go with it, each client's projects and the way into code.

sections.title: Clients and their design sets
sections.body: Colours with role and print values, fonts with their licence, logos with their ground, type sizes, rules and example files. Every colour shows its steps from 50 to 950 and its contrast with white and dark.

sections.title: Versions on a timeline
sections.where: At the top of a client's page, History tab
sections.body: Every change starts as a draft; it is published with the day it is valid from and stays as it is after that. “As of” shows any day, “3 years ago” is one click. Two versions side by side show what changed.

sections.title: Projects with a CI of their own
sections.where: A client's Projects tab, then “New project”
sections.body: An app, a product or a campaign gets versions of its own on a version of the client. For each part you decide: as the client, as the client plus its own, or entirely its own. When the client gets a new version, the project stays where it is until you move it with “Move to …”.

sections.title: Dark mode as part of the CI
sections.where: In a draft, Colours tab, “Suggest a dark mode”
sections.body: nexbrand suggests ground, surface, text, muted text, main colour and text on it for dark pages from the palette. You adjust the mapping, the checks include it, the export carries it, and preview and review switch between light and dark.

sections.title: Checks and rules that are computed
sections.where: A client's Checks and Rules tabs, and Contrast in the top bar
sections.body: Contrast of every combination by WCAG 2.2, logos at 3:1, colour vision deficiencies, nearly identical colours, text that is too small, fonts that must not leave the house. Rules for colour pairs, logo grounds and fonts are checked, for programs through the API and MCP too; free rules stay text for people. The contrast calculator suggests the nearest colour of the same hue that is enough.

sections.title: Create a new CI and agree on it
sections.where: New client, top right; then the Review tab
sections.body: Start from a few words, a picture, a colour or nothing. The workbench suggests colour schemes, neutrals, a font pair and sizes, with a sample page and the checks running alongside. The directions go to the client by link, by mail too if you like. The client pages through your drafts at full size, comments on each picture and chooses; that choice becomes version 1.0. What the client writes is counted on the tab and in the client list until someone of yours opens the review.

sections.title: Collect from a website, repo or PDF
sections.body: Colours, fonts and logos are measured and sorted, by rules or with your own AI. The result becomes a draft, or you check a page against the CI and find the nearly right shades. The operator allows websites and repos under Settings, Server, Collecting and AI.

sections.title: As code, through the API and MCP
sections.where: “As code” on a client's page; tokens under My account, Connections
sections.body: Every version as CSS variables, a Tailwind 4 theme, SCSS or design tokens, on the public page for developers without an account too. Programs read through /api/v1, an AI in an editor through MCP. By default a token covers only the clients you choose and lasts 90 days; one of the level “Read and propose drafts” writes a redesign back, always as a draft.

small: Public links show a design set read-only, a fixed version or always the current one, with an expiry date and a password. Everyone who may write for a client creates and sees its links.
Client, project and team names exist only once; nexbrand says so as you create them.
A blocked account learns at sign-in that it is blocked and whom to ask. The block dialog names the open client links of the person, with a button to withdraw them.
Team leads change their teams only when the operator allows it (Settings, Teams).
Notices speak to you directly, numbers come in the right singular and plural, and every message from the server is a whole sentence in your language.
Accounts, second factor, sign-in through OIDC with the authentik button, log, own languages and backups.
For a move to a new server, upload a downloaded backup there (Settings, Server, Backups, “Upload a backup”). It joins the list: check it first, then restore it.
